Sage Gautama called out to Aruni, who responded from the breach.

Sage Gautama blessed Uddalaka with knowledge of all Vedas and law codes for his obedience.
Uddalaka departed to go where he wished after receiving the blessing.
Sage Gautama sent his other disciple Upamanyu to tend the cows.
Sage Gautama noticed Upamanyu's obesity and questioned him about his sustenance.
Upamanyu revealed he lived by begging, but Sage Gautama forbade him from eating without offering first.
Upamanyu continued begging twice and offering to his teacher, but was criticized for harming others' livelihoods.
Upamanyu revealed he sustained himself on cow's milk without permission, receiving further disapproval.
Upamanyu continued obeying and returning to his teacher after tending cows.

Upamanyu explained to the teacher that he survived by eating the foam sprayed when calves suckled their mothers' milk.
The teacher told Upamanyu that the virtuous calves sprayed foam out of pity, but consuming it would harm them, so he should not even eat the foam.
Upamanyu agreed and stopped eating, tending to cows while restricted from begged food, second begging, milk, and milk foam.
